question.text: An AIF sponsor is comparing the Trust versus the LLP versus the Company route. Which of the following is a genuine downside of using an LLP structure for an AIF in India?

answer.text: An LLP cannot be a taxable entity under the Income-tax Act
An LLP is not permitted to raise capital commitments from foreign investors
An LLP cannot have more than 50 partners as per the LLP Act 2008
LLP investors become partners, and their details come into public domain via MCA filings, losing the secrecy of a trust

explanation.text: The Logic: In an LLP-structured AIF, investors are partners. MCA filings put their details in the public domain, so the privacy that a trust structure offers is lost. The Trap: Option A is wrong — LLPs are taxable entities under the Income-tax Act. Option B is false — LLPs may accept foreign capital subject to applicable conditions. Option C confuses the old partnership-firm cap; the LLP Act 2008 has no such 50-partner limit. Note: Investor anonymity is a common reason sponsors choose the trust route over an LLP for AIFs.
